angle.description: Required original human angle (PRD R4, D-018).

closing_question.description: The SINGLE specific topical question the video ends on ('Which hour would you hand over first?'). Not engagement-begging (STYLE_GUIDE §9) — one question, one topic. build-metadata seeds the pinned comment from it (Phase 1.3).

pinned_comment.description: Optional authored pinned-comment text that ANSWERS the closing_question and invites replies ('Mine was copy-paste. What's yours?'). When omitted, build-metadata derives an invite from closing_question.

short_hook.description: Purpose-built opener for the Short. The Short no longer inherits the long-form hook: when present, make-short PREPENDS this as the Short's first scene so the first ~3s is authored for Short psychology ('Everyone thinks AI takes jobs. It doesn't.'). Respects one-continuous-audio — its narration is voiced as part of the Short's own TTS pass, never spliced from the long track.

narration.description: The Short's purpose-built opening spoken line(s) — its own cold-open, not the long-form intro.

sentences.description: Sentence split of narration (defaults to [narration] when omitted).

on_screen_text.description: The visual/caption punch shown over the first spoken line — preferred mechanism: a strong on-screen line distinct from the VO.

component.description: Optional bespoke hook-* component name (must start with 'hook' to satisfy the hook-class QA gate). When set the opener renders as a custom hero instead of a hook-card.

short_cuts.description: 1B (D-074): the 2-3 Shorts cut from THIS long video's own scenes — make-shorts.mjs turns each into a unit (short, short-2, short-3) that reuses the scenes' HyperFrames renders in portrait, with their narration voiced again as the Short's own track. An editorial call by the script writer: each cut must stand alone in ~45-60 s.

title.description: The Short's working title (its own hook, not the long's).

scenes.description: Long scene ids, in the order the Short plays them. Each scene belongs to one cut. Without a hook, the first one is the cold open.

opening.description: Replaces the FIRST sentence of the first listed scene — one sentence for one, so the scene's beats still land — when the long's line leans on what came before ('So…', 'Then…', 'in this video').

hook.description: Optional purpose-built opener voiced before the scenes.

hf_scene.description: The portrait HyperFrames scene the hook renders with (templates/hyperframes/scenes/<name>).

closing_question.description: The Short's own closing question, when the long's does not fit it.

capture_id.description: Set only for capture-segment scenes (mini-demo). The scene's PRIMARY clip.

capture_ids.description: Optional: every clip a capture-segment scene draws on, in beat order, when one scene cuts between several takes (016 s6: before → run → after). capture_id stays the primary; the scene-plan's beats bind one id each.

pause_after.description: Optional scripted silence: hold a beat by splicing real silence into the narration after a sentence. Sentence-final punctuation only buys ~0.4s, so a designed hold (016 s6, the moment before the run) has to be synthesized. scripts/make_voice.py cuts the track into segments at each pause and shifts every later timestamp; the scene window widens to match.

key_takes.description: Optional: indexes into THIS scene's sentences[] that are KEY TAKES — the lines the viewer must remember. scripts/make_voice.py (and make_voice_azure.py) speak them at brief.voice_rate_key instead of brief.voice_rate so they have time to land; a scene can also read them to settle its motion and highlight the take (024 Short, 2026-10-09).
